title: Maintain your own scorecard
coreMove: Measure against the standard you can defend when public scores misread the work.
sourcePressure: Failure section: self-honest standards replacing external validation. Supported by frozen TOC and book skeleton; no per-chapter source sidecar exists in the latest run.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Turning the scorecard into private self-flattery rather than a stricter standard than applause or blame.
sourceAnchorNote: No named person, study, place, or artifact is available in the frozen source sidecar for this chapter; use fictional scenarios only and do not invent source anecdotes.

hook: opening with a generic definition of scorecard
starting with a neat ambition maxim
counterintuition: not a simple scorecard is good/bad reversal
not a success is secretly dangerous template
tryThisNow: take a deep breath before responding

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside only if source-supported, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference where source anchors allow it
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
